title: WPPIL/121/2017 of Mohd Nasir AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Delay Condonation application in Short Counter Affdiavit No. 15784 of 2017
In
Writ Petition (PIL) No. 121 of 2017
Mohd. Nasir and another .......... Petitioners

Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others .......... Respondents
No representation for the petitioners.
Mr. Anil Kumar Bisht, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand/respondent nos. 1
to 4.
Dated : 07th December, 2017

Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.

K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)
Delay in filing the short counter affidavit on behalf of respondent no.
2 is condoned. Short counter affidavit is taken on record. Delay
condonation application is allowed.
2. The prayer sought in the writ petition is to take appropriate action for
shifting the Composite Liquor Shop of respondent no. 5 from Ramnagar
Road Kashipur to the original place of allotment as per the condition of the
Allotment Order.
3. Briefly put, the case of the petitioner is as follows:
 The private respondent, who was allotted the Composite Liquor
Shop, has illegally, and without approval of the District Magistrate, shifted
his shop from Pratappur Kichha to Ramnagar Road, Kashipur. The private
respondent was allotted the shop at Pratappur and not at Kashipur.
4. A short counter affidavit has been filed, wherein it is stated as
follows:
"4. That it is respectfully submitted that an illegal Composite
Liquor shop was being run by the respondent no.5 on Pratapur

2
Road/Ramnagar Road by the license holder, taking cognizance
whereof, the deponent time and again warned the licensee that
only after the conversion of Composite Liquor Shop into
English Liquor Shop from the Government/Commissionary,
the operation of a liquor shop is permissible in the said
premised. Despite that the licensee did not take any interest on
transferring the liquor shop outside the ambit of Nagar Nigam
area rather he continue to operate the Composite Liquor Shop
in the prohibited area of Nagar Nigam, Kashipur and despite
service of notice of violation of law and order, when the
licensee did not shift its shop, the answering respondent has
got the said Composite Liquor Shop sealed on 1-11-2017 at
about 2:00 P.M. and the information in this regard has also
been given to the Joint Magistrate/S.D.M. Kashipur and
concerned Circle Officer of Police, Kashipur, and the said
Composite Liquor Shop is closed now. Copy of the order dated
01-11-2017 is being enclosed herewith and marked as
Annexure SCA-1 to this affidavit."
5. The petitioner was given time to file rejoinder affidavit. There is no
rejoinder affidavit filed.
6. In the circumstances, we see no reason not to place reliance on the
statement contained in the short counter affidavit.
7. Accordingly, the complaint of the petitioner does not survive and the
writ petition is closed.
